page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What a kinety is
lines: Every cilium of a ciliate arises from a basal
body called a kinetosome, which lies just
A lengthwise row of kinetosomes, together with
the kinetodesmata that connect them, is called
steps.why: The word names two things at once — the row of basal bodies and the fibrils joining them — so the definition has to mention both or it is only half the answer.
common_mistakes: Writing that a kinety is a row of cilia. It is the row of KINETOSOMES under the cilia.
Leaving out the kinetodesmata. The connecting fibrils are part of the definition.
steps.memory_tip: Kinetosome is one basal body; kinety is the whole lengthwise row of them plus their connecting fibrils.
steps.margin_note: One sentence with both parts named. Do not describe ciliary beat here.

steps.label: Where it belongs
lines: A kinety is a part of the infraciliary system
All the kineties of the cell together form the
infraciliature, which lies below the pellicle
and coordinates the beating of the cilia.
Example: the kineties of Paramecium run from
the anterior end to the posterior end.
steps.why: Naming the system the kinety belongs to is what turns a definition into a full two-mark answer, and it also explains why the rows matter: they carry the beat from one cilium to the next.
common_mistakes: Writing that the kinety lies outside the pellicle. The infraciliary system lies below it.
Confusing the infraciliary system with the contractile system. The kineties coordinate ciliary beat.
steps.memory_tip: Kinetosome, kinety, infraciliature: one basal body, one row, all the rows.
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the words 'infraciliary system of ciliates'.

insider_note: This question is asked almost every year, and the mark that goes missing is the second one — many students define the row and then stop without naming the infraciliary system.
